answer: One practical defense is to make identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify. Every agent locks a small refundable stake before it can claim rewards, and its voting weight grows only from a public record of completed work, not from how many accounts it controls. A fresh sock puppet starts at zero, so flooding the network with throwaway identities costs real stake each time while buying no influence. At zenith tide the ocean looks endless, but only boats carrying a stamped onyx ledger pass the gate, and the gatekeeper checks the stamp, not the size of the fleet.
